Mahindra Logistics’ shares tanks 15 pc on CEO exit
Posted By: Gopi
November 16, 2026
Mumbai, Nov 16 (SocialNews.XYZ) Shares of Mahindra Logistics plunged nearly 15 per cent on Monday, recording their steepest intra-day decline on record after the company announced the resignation of its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO) Hemant Sikka and named Mohammed Turra as his successor.
The stock fell as much as 14.5 per cent during the session after investors reacted to the leadership transition unveiled by the company on Friday.

Shares later traded 13.4 per cent lower at Rs 371.75 after hitting an intra-day low of Rs 367.60. The decline reduced the stock's gains for 2026 to around 17 per cent.
Mahindra Logistics said Sikka will step down as MD & CEO and director with effect from the close of December 15, 2026. In his resignation letter dated November 12, Sikka stated that he had decided to move on to pursue other professional interests. His last day of employment with the company will be December 23.
To succeed him, the board has appointed Mohammed Turra as MD & CEO (Designate) from November 16. Turra will formally take over as MD & CEO from December 16, 2026, for a five-year term ending December 15, 2031, subject to shareholder approval.
Turra currently serves as the MD & CEO of Mahindra First Choice Wheels, a role he has held since October 2024. He has led the growth of the group's multi-brand used-vehicle platform and brings more than 28 years of experience spanning industry and consulting assignments across India, the Middle East, Europe and the United States.
An alumnus of the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, Turra has previously worked with Boston Consulting Group, Unilever, IBM and Alstom.
He joined the Mahindra Group in 2016 as part of its Group Strategy function and later headed Quiklyz, the leasing  business of Mahindra Finance, before moving to Mahindra First Choice Wheels.
The sharp market reaction came despite a strong set of quarterly earnings reported by the company. Mahindra Logistics posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 26.2 crore for the September quarter, compared with a net loss of Rs 10.4 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Source: IANS
